title: Whether records spread the copying
summary: Barry suggests recordings of George Lewis and others made copying possible worldwide; Joe heard many clarinetists as a boy.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I suppose the recordings had a lot to do with it, because I mean, for someone like... Let's go back to... You were talking about Isadore Fritz. Now, Isadore Fritz probably was only heard in the little places in the South where he traveled, whereas George Lewis, for instance, or
Barney or any of them, recorded, so you could hear how George Lewis played in Yugoslavia or in Santiago, Chile. I suppose that perhaps had something to do with it.
I had listened to so many different kinds of clarinet players when I was little, and so many of them sound good, you know.
